A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same interruption study. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, output-length, interruption, and model-scaling experiments in Sections 4–6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and adds comparator evaluations, robustness analyses, and human validation in Sections 6.3–6.4 and Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: The hard, soft, and update-driven interruption procedures and the prompt-guidance intervention already appear in v1 and remain in v4. The paraphrase ablation, additional comparators, and proprietary-model proxy do not establish a revision to the proposed core method.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, MATH500, AIME24/25, and LiveCodeBench-v6, including their augmented update-driven problems. The added controls, model evaluations, and annotation checks use this existing coverage; no additional application domain or benchmark task is evaluated.

E2.justification: v4 evaluates Chain of Draft against ordinary Qwen3-8B reasoning under all three interruption modes (Section 6.4); v1 only cites it. Appendix F.2 also adds evaluated DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama and Nemotron-3-Nano comparisons beyond the original model families, substantially expanding the comparative evidence.

E3.justification: v4 adds paragraph-boundary interruption experiments, an augmented-problem/no-update control, larger model configurations, and a GPT-5.4-Mini proxy with internal reasoning disabled. Human validation introduces two 50-sample checks and multiple panic thresholds. Appendix F.4 re-bins existing runs by absolute character length; it does not establish new fixed-token-budget experiments.

E4.justification: New analyses test guidance paraphrasing, possible benchmark memorization, interruption boundaries, and dependence on relative indexing. Appendix E adds panic-threshold sensitivity and human checks of panic and self-doubt labels. The original scaling, turn-role, and speedup analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix E newly reports coefficients of variation across panic thresholds and human agreement estimates for the automated labels. Both versions retain 16 AIME trials, single runs elsewhere, and bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals; v4 does not establish increased repeated-run counts or specify a new significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive model, comparator, and robustness results, including 90% panic-label agreement and 88% self-doubt-label agreement in Appendix E. Section 6.4 newly reports AIME panic rates of 13.1% with Chain of Draft versus 3.8% with regular reasoning at position 0.3. Existing LiveCodeBench update-driven curves also change substantially in Figures 4, 6, and 8, without an explanation establishing whether these are corrections or reruns.

T1.justification: The inference formalization, interruption-conditioned accuracy and length definitions, and necessary-update condition in Section 3 are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs; the new operational labeling criteria and empirical analyses do not revise the mathematical framework.

C1.justification: v4 modestly narrows the contribution framing from a new analytical framework for persistent interruptible agents to an evaluation setting, benchmark, and error taxonomy, explicitly emphasizing single-round experiments. The central claims about dynamic fragility, the three failure modes, and drops of up to 60% remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive interpretations concerning memorization controls, prompt sensitivity, problem difficulty, and why compact reasoning does not eliminate interruption failures. It narrows the coding-fragility discussion particularly to Qwen3 and explains that the proprietary-API proxy cannot establish native-reasoning behavior. The limitations also clarify the diagnostic scope and requirements for future interruption-aware training.

D1.justification: v4 discloses the 1% remaining-context panic criterion, GPT-5 self-doubt classification, annotation sample counts, a paraphrased guidance prompt, and the dataset acceptance rate. It specifies an MIT license and replaces the dataset-collection link with a direct benchmark-dataset link. The original prompts and general hardware/hyperparameter descriptions largely remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds model and software references, including Nemotron-3-Nano, GPT-5.2, Gemini 3, SillyTavern, and text-generation-webui. It explicitly connects the study to Chain of Draft through evaluation, while retaining the overall positioning against efficient reasoning under static contexts.

P1.justification: The overall narrative sequence and much existing prose remain. v4 revises the abstract, contribution bullets, experimental rationale, and conclusion; separates limitations from the conclusion; and adds an impact statement and human-validation appendix. These are localized editorial and structural changes rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v4 converts the main paper to a two-column conference layout, substantially resizing and relocating existing multi-panel figures. It adds baseline and robustness figures, extensive appendix plots, and two validation tables. The original appendix plots are matched to Figures F.23–F.27, with some revised displays and results.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens support for the central diagnoses: Appendix E validates previously insufficiently documented failure labels, while the new controls, interruption analyses, and Chain of Draft comparison address important alternative explanations left open in v1. Broader model evidence and explicit proxy limitations further improve credibility. Small validation samples, overgeneralization from one paraphrase, and crowded figures remain weaknesses, but the net evidential improvement is substantial.
